title: Describing changes over time / Kyerεw ka a wɔde akyi akyi
bridge: Wɔ Twirekronkan, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama nnwuma a wɔde akyi akyi, woatɔn 'get', 'become' ne 'turn' a wɔn ho asɛm wɔ Hɔwyɛɛkronkan ma amo a wɔde akyi akyi kyerεw no ho asɛm no ase. Afei nti, Twirekronkan mmom no, wɔmmusua 'be' anaa 'am' ne adwuma a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase; na wɔde nnwuma a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase. Afei nti, Twirekronkan no kyerεw ka a wɔde akyi akyi no ne present perfect ('have changed') ne past simple ('changed') a wɔn ho asɛm wɔ Hɔwyɛɛkronkan ma amo a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase. Afei nti, ako a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no, wɔde 'estoy más cansado' kyerεw 'I am more tired' na ɛnne 'I have gotten more tired'.
rule: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama nnwuma a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase: 1) Tɔn 'get' + adwuma (anaa comparativo) sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama nnwuma a wɔde akyi akyi anaa a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase: 'get older', 'get better', 'get colder'. 2) Tɔn 'become' + adwuma/adwuma sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama nnwuma a wɔde akyi akyi anaa a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase: 'become a teacher', 'become famous'. 3) Tɔn 'turn' + color anaa adwuma sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama nnwuma a wɔde akyi akyi anaa a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase: 'turn red', 'turn pale'. 4) Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama nnwuma a wɔde akyi akyi anaa a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase, tɔn 'grow' (crecer) ne 'fall' (caer) wɔ nnwuma a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase: 'grow old', 'fall asleep'. 5) Tɔn 'used to' sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama nnwuma a wɔde akyi akyi anaa a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase: 'I used to live here'. 6) Tɔn 'no longer' ne 'still' sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama nnwuma a wɔde akyi akyi anaa a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase: 'I no longer smoke', 'I still work here'. 7) Tɔn present perfect sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama nnwuma a wɔde akyi akyi anaa a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase: 'The town has changed a lot'. Mmom, wɔmmusua 'be' anaa 'am' + adwuma sɛ wɔde Hɔwyɛɛkronkan no ho asɛm no ase: 'estoy cansado' nni 'I am tired' sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama nnwuma a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase, na 'I have gotten tired'.

common_error.wrong: I am more tired now than before.
common_error.correct: I have gotten more tired now.
common_error.correct_alt: I have become more tired now.
common_error.explanation: Asɛm no adi sɛ wɔde 'estoy más cansado' kyerεw a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase. Nanso, wɔ Twirekronkan, 'I am tired' kyerεw a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase, na ɛnne a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase, tɔn present perfect ne 'get' anaa 'become' (anaa 'have gotten' / 'have become'). Wɔde 'I am more tired' kyerεw sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase, nanso ɛnne a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase. Mfa kyerεw a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase ne sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama a wɔde akyi akyi anaa a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase.

examples.original: It is getting colder.
examples.phonetic: /ɪt ɪz ˈɡetɪŋ ˈkoʊldər/
examples.translation: Ɛyɛ adɔm a wɔde akyi akyi (ɛyɛ adɔm a wɔde akyi akyi).
examples.note: Tɔn 'get' + comparativo sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama nnwuma a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase. Wɔ Hɔwyɛɛkronkan, wɔde 'está haciendo' kyerεw a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase, nanso wɔ Twirekronkan, wɔde 'is getting' kyerεw a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no asese.

examples.original: My English is getting better.

examples.original: The days are getting longer.
examples.phonetic: /ðə deɪz ɑːr ˈɡetɪŋ ˈlɔːŋɡər/

examples.original: He became famous after the video.
examples.phonetic: /hi bɪˈkeɪm ˈfeɪməs ˈæftər ðə ˈvɪdi.oʊ/
examples.translation: Ɔno ayɛ apam a wɔde akyi akyi akyerε video no ho asɛm.
examples.note: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama nnwuma a wɔde akyi akyi (apam, apam) no ho asɛm no ase, tɔn 'become'. Wɔ Hɔwyɛɛkronkan, wɔde 'hacerse' kyerεw no ho asɛm.

examples.original: The situation became complicated.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən bɪˈkeɪm ˈkɑːmplɪkeɪtɪd/
examples.translation: Asɛm no ayɛ kɔntɔnkron a wɔde akyi akyi.

examples.original: She became a doctor in 2010.
examples.phonetic: /ʃi bɪˈkeɪm ə ˈdɑːktər ɪn tuː ˈθaʊzənd ˈtɛn/
examples.translation: Ɔno ayɛ adwuma a wɔde akyi akyi wɔ 2010.
examples.note: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama nnwuma anaa adwuma a wɔde akyi akyi no ho asɛm no ase, tɔn 'become' + adwuma a wɔn ho asɛm no nni.

examples.original: She didn't use to smoke, but now she does.

examples.note: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama nnwuma a wɔn ho asɛm no nni no ho asɛm no ase, tɔn 'didn't use to' (nni '-d' wɔ 'use' no mu). Hwɛ sɛ wopɛ sɛ woaboa ama /juːst/ no ho asɛm no ase.

title: Speculating and making deductions / Adwuma ne ahoɔden
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, yɛnka 'debe de ser' anaa 'puede que sea' maa adwuma ne ahoɔden. Wɔ English mu, yɛnka 'must', 'might', 'could', 'can't' + infinitive. Nokware no, 'must' ka ahoɔden a ɛyɛ den pii (positive) na 'can't' ka ahoɔden a ɛyɛ mframa; 'might', 'may' ne 'could' ka ahoɔden a ɛyɛ akɔnnɔ. Nya awerɛhow: mmom hwee 'must not' maa ahoɔden a ɛfiri so, efisɛ wɔ English mu, 'must not' ka kyerɛkyerɛ a wɔatwa wo nsa.
rule: Ma wɔadwuma ne ahoɔden wɔ present tense wɔ English mu, yɛnka modals no a wɔatwa so: 'must' (ahoɔden a ɛyɛ den sɛ biribi yɛ nokware), 'can't' (ahoɔden a ɛyɛ den sɛ biribi yɛ mframa), 'might', 'may', 'could' (ahoɔden a ɛyɛ akɔnnɔ, ɛnyɛ den pii). Ma wɔka ho asɛm wɔ past tense mu, yɛnka 'must have + past participle', 'can't have + past participle', 'might have + past participle', etc. Kyerɛkyerɛ no ne: subject + modal + base verb (present) anaa modal + have + past participle (past). Nnipa: wɔ Twi mu, 'debe de ser' ne 'no puede ser' yɛ adwuma mfirinhyia, nanso wɔ English mu, wɔnka 'must not be' maa ahoɔden a ɛfiri so; wɔnka 'can't be'.

concept_examples.text: He must be tired after the long trip.
concept_examples.translation: Ɔno debe de ser anim sɛ ɔbɛyɛ adansefo a ɔyɛ den pii.
concept_examples.phonetic: /hiː mʌst biː ˈtaɪərd ˈæftər ðə lɔːŋ trɪp/

concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃiː kænt biː ˈsɪriəs əˈbaʊt ˈmuːvɪŋ tuː əˈnʌðər ˈkʌntri/

concept_examples.text: It could rain later, so take an umbrella.
concept_examples.translation: Ɔkɔm hyɛ sɛ ɔbɛbɔ abɔ nea ɛbɛyɛ a, na ɛno a, sɛe adwuma.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪt kʊd reɪn ˈleɪtər soʊ teɪk ən ʌmˈbrelə/

common_error.wrong: He must not be at home because the lights are off.
common_error.correct: He can't be at home because the lights are off.
common_error.correct_alt: He must be out because the lights are off.
common_error.explanation: Ɛbɔ nea ɛyɛ a, wɔ Twi mu, wɔka 'no debe estar' maa ahoɔden a ɛyɛ mframa, nanso wɔ English mu, 'must not' ka kyerɛkyerɛ a wɔatwa wo nsa ('no debe' = wɔmmra wo nsa). Ma wɔbɔ ahoɔden sɛ biribi yɛ mframa anaa ɛyɛ nokware, wɔnka 'can't' (anaa 'couldn't' sɛ wɔpɛ sɛ ɛbɛyɛ fɔɔ). 'Must be out' no yɛ nokware efisɛ ɛne 'can't be at home' yɛ adwuma mfirinhyia.

examples.original: You're a journalist. You must meet a lot of people.

examples.note: Yɛnka 'must' sɛ yɛpɛ sɛ yɛbɔ ahoɔden a ɛyɛ den pii efisɛ yɛnni hɔ. Wɔ Twi mu, 'debe de'.

examples.original: That can't be the right answer.
examples.phonetic: /ðæt kænt biː ðə raɪt ˈænsər/
examples.translation: Ɛnyɛ nokware sɛ ɛno ne kwan a ɛyɛ den.
examples.note: Yɛnka 'can't' sɛ yɛpɛ sɛ yɛka sɛ biribi yɛ mframa. Wɔ Twi mu, 'no puede ser'.

examples.original: He must have a lot of money because he drives a Ferrari.

examples.note: Yɛnka 'because' (efisɛ) ma yɛde ahoɔden no hyɛn.

levels.label: Possibility with might, may, and could
levels.translation: Ahoɔden a ɛyɛ akɔnnɔ ne might, may ne could

examples.translation: Puede que esté en el gimnasio ahora mismo.
examples.note: 'Might' ka ahoɔden a ɛyɛ akɔnnɔ sɛ 'must'. Wɔ Twi mu, 'puede que'.

examples.original: They may arrive late because of the traffic.

examples.note: 'May' ne 'might' yɛ adwuma mfirinhyia, nanso 'may' yɛ fɔɔ sɛn bi. Mmom, wɔno nyinaa yɛ nokware.

examples.original: This could be the best restaurant in the city.
examples.phonetic: /ðɪs kʊd biː ðə best ˈrestərɒnt ɪn ðə ˈsɪti/
examples.translation: ɛno ne restaurant a ɛyɛ den pii wɔ ɛno mu.
examples.note: 'Could' ne ahoɔden a ɛyɛ akɔnnɔ na wɔnka no pii wɔ kasa mu.

examples.original: He must have studied a lot for the exam.
examples.phonetic: /hiː mʌst hæv ˈstʌdid ə lɒt fɔːr ði ɪɡˈzæm/
examples.translation: Ɔno debe de haber estudiado mucho para el examen.
examples.note: Yɛnka 'must have + past participle' ma yɛbɔ ahoɔden wɔ past tense mu. Wɔ Twi mu, 'debe de haber'.

examples.original: She can't have seen us because she didn't wave.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː kænt hæv siːn ʌs bɪˈkɒz ʃiː dɪdnt weɪv/
examples.translation: Ɛnyɛ nokware sɛ wɔahunahuna yɛn efisɛ wɔmmra wo nsa.
examples.note: 'Can't have + past participle' ka ahoɔden a ɛyɛ mframa wɔ past tense mu. Wɔ Twi mu, 'no puede haber'.

examples.original: They might have missed the bus.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ maɪt hæv mɪst ðə bʌs/
examples.translation: Puede que hayan perdido el autobús.
examples.note: 'Might have + past participle' ka ahoɔden a ɛyɛ akɔnnɔ wɔ past tense mu. Wɔ Twi mu, 'puede que hayan'.

examples.original: The roads are wet. It must have rained.
examples.phonetic: /ðə roʊdz ɑːr wet. ɪt mʌst hæv reɪnd/
examples.translation: Adan no yɛ mframa. Ɔno debe de haber llovido.
examples.note: Nokware a ɛyɛ den (adan no yɛ mframa) ma yɛbɔ ahoɔden a ɛyɛ den wɔ past tense mu.

title: Expressing regret and hypothetical situations / Kyerɛw wo nsa na nsɛmmiso a edidi so
bridge: Wɔ Twiriso, woyɛ kondisional ne subhuntivo ho asɛm sɛdeɛ wɔhyɛ hypothesis ne regret (sɛdeɛ, 'si tuviera tiempo, iría'). Wɔ English, structure no yɛ fɔɔ: wɔhyɛ ahyɛdeɛ a efifir (anaa ahyɛdeɛ a efi nea ɛfata) wɔ 'if' clause ne 'would' + verb wɔ main clause. Common error bi ka sɛ wɔbɛtrɛ 'si tendría' si 'if I would have', nanso wɔ English, 'if' clause no mmom nni 'would'. Enti, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka nsɛmmiso a edidi so wɔ ahyɛdeɛ a efi nea ɛfata, wɔhyɛ ahyɛdeɛ a efi nea ɛfata ('had + participle') na ɛnnyɛ conditional compound.
rule: Wɔ English B1, sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka hypothesis a wɔ present anaa future (second conditional), wɔhyɛ 'if + ahyɛdeɛ a efifir' (anaw 'if + ahyɛdeɛ a efi nea ɛyɛ') wɔ conditional clause, ne 'would + base form' wɔ main clause. Sɛdeɛ: 'If I had more time, I would travel.' (Sɛ mawo adi a mepɛ, mɛkɔ). Fa so sɛ 'were' wɔhyɛ wɔn ho wɔ 'if I were' (nanso 'was' yɛ common wɔ informal English). Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woka regret about the past (third conditional), wɔhyɛ 'if + ahyɛdeɛ a efi nea ɛfata' (had + participle) ne 'would have + participle' wɔ main clause: 'If I had studied, I would have passed.' (Sɛ mɛto asɛm no, mɛfa). Wohwɛ sɛ wɔhyɛ 'I wish' + ahyɛdeɛ a efi nea ɛfata maa regret: 'I wish I had studied.' (Mepɛ sɛ mɛto asɛm no). Fa so sɛ 'if' clause no nni 'would' anaa 'will'. Wɔ formal hypothesis, 'were' yɛ paa: 'If he were here...'.

concept_examples.text: If I had more money, I would buy a car.
concept_examples.translation: Sɛ mawo adi a mepɛ, mɛto baako.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ hæd mɔːr ˈmʌni aɪ wʊd baɪ ə kɑːr/

concept_examples.text: I wish I knew the answer.
concept_examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ mihwɛ ahoɔden no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɪʃ aɪ nuː ði ˈænsər/

concept_examples.text: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
concept_examples.translation: Sɛ ɔkaa no ato asɛm a efata, ɔbɛfa apam no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf ʃiː hæd ˈstʌdid ˈhɑːrdər ʃiː wʊd hæv pæst ði ɪɡˈzæm/

concept_examples.text: I would travel more if I were younger.
concept_examples.translation: Mɛkɔ adi a mepɛ sɛ mɛyɛ deɛ mepɛ sɛ miyɛ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd ˈtrævl mɔːr ɪf aɪ wɜːr ˈjʌŋɡər/

common_error.wrong: If I would have time, I would go to the party.
common_error.correct: If I had time, I would go to the party.
common_error.correct_alt: If I had time, I'd go to the party.
common_error.explanation: Error no baa nti wɔ Twiriso, yɛka 'si tendría tiempo' (conditional), nanso wɔ English, 'if' clause no nni 'would'. Na yɛhyɛ ahyɛdeɛ a efifir (had). Maa woyɛ error no, fa so sɛ 'if' twa ahyɛdeɛ a efifir (maa hypothesis a wɔ present/future) anaa ahyɛdeɛ a efi nea ɛfata (maa past), na 'would' mmom wɔ nea ɛho clause no.

examples.original: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ wʌn ðə ˈlɑːtəri aɪ wʊd ˈtrævl ðə wɜːrld/
examples.translation: Sɛ mafa apam no, mɛkɔ world no so.
examples.note: Fa so sɛ 'won' yɛ ahyɛdeɛ a efifir, na ɛmmfiri 'ganó' wɔ hɛn.

examples.original: If he were taller, he could play basketball.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf hiː wɜːr ˈtɔːlər hiː kʊd pleɪ ˈbæskɪtbɔːl/
examples.translation: Sɛ miyɛ paa, mɛtɔ so akatua.
examples.note: Wɔ formal English, wɔhyɛ 'were' maa wɔn nyinaa, nanso 'was' yɛ common wɔ informal.

examples.original: What would you do if you had a million dollars?
examples.phonetic: /wʌt wʊd juː duː ɪf juː hæd ə ˈmɪljən ˈdɑːlərz/
examples.translation: Deɛ wɔbɛyɛ sɛ wɔde million dollars bi ma wo?
examples.note: Question no twa 'would' ne subject no.

examples.original: If I had known, I would have come earlier.

title: Discussing Advantages and Disadvantages / Kasa mmusuo ne mmerɛ
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnka 'mmusuo' ne 'mmerɛ' sɛ mmusuo, nanso wɔ English, wɔnka 'advantages' ne 'disadvantages' sɛ mmusuo pɛpɛɛpɛ a wɔhyɛ wɔn ho asɛm wɔ verb 'have' anaa 'there are' ho. Enti, wɔ English, wɔka 'pros and cons' wɔ nkyekyem asɛm ho, sɛɛ wɔ Twi nni sɛɛ no ho asɛm. Nhyira wo nti, woma ntumi adi 'por un lado' sɛ 'for one side' – asɛm bu no ne 'on the one hand'.
rule:
Saa wopɛ sɛ woka mmusuo ne mmerɛ wɔ English a, hwɛ mmerɛ no:
1. 'One advantage (of) is that...' / 'One disadvantage (of) is that...' – na wɔhyɛ clause bi a ɛwɔ subject ne verb so.
2. 'The advantages of + noun/gerund are...' ma wɔatwa so.
3. 'On the one hand... on the other hand...' ma wɔakyerɛkyerɛ mmusuo mmienu.
4. 'However' anaa 'Nevertheless' ma wɔato so mmerɛ no akyi a wɔakasa mmusuo no.
5. 'Pros and cons' ne asɛm kɛse a ɛwɔ mmusuo pɛpɛɛpɛ: 'Let's weigh the pros and cons.'
Nka sɛ wɔ English, wɔnnhyɛ 'of' akyi 'advantage' sɛ wɔnni noun a ɛbɛba akyi no: 'It has many advantages' (nni 'advantages of').

title: Narrating a story / Kasa asɛm bi
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛka asɛm a ɛda hyɛ no, yɛnkyɛn yɛnara so ama a, yɛde ɛkɔso kyerɛw kronkron ne ɛkɔso a ɛrekɔ da no. Wɔ English, ɛkyɛn kyɛn, nanso ɛwom mframa: 'past simple' de ama a a ɛda hyɛ no, na 'past continuous' de ama a a ɛrekɔ da wɔ bere a ɛda hyɛ no. Ɛyɛ den a wɔde 'estaba + gerundio' kyerɛw kronkron a ɛde no wɔ Spanish wɔ English, nanso wɔ English, wɔde 'used to' anaa 'would' kyerɛw ama a a ɛda hyɛ no a ɛnyɛ kwan paa wɔ Spanish. Sɛe: wɔ English, 'past perfect' (had + participio) de ama a a ɛda hyɛ no pɛn pɛn wɔ kasa kyerɛw no ho wɔ Spanish a wɔfrɛ no 'pluscuamperfecto'.
rule:
Sɛ wubɛka asɛm bi wɔ English wɔ B1 level no, ebia wuhwɛ mma ɛkɔso kyerɛw nnɛmba no:
1. **Past Simple** (kyerɛkyerɛ: ɔkyerɛfoɔ + ɛkɔso a ɛda hyɛ no, e.i. 'walked'; kyerɛkyerɛ mmienu: 'didn't + ɛkɔso'; kyerɛkyerɛ kɔkɔ: 'Did + ɔkyerɛfoɔ + ɛkɔso?). Wɔde no kyerɛ ama a a ɛda hyɛ no ne a ɛrekɔ da wɔ ɛkɔso kronkron.
2. **Past Continuous** (was/were + ɛkɔso -ing). Kyerɛ ama a ɛrekɔ da wɔ bere bi a ɛda hyɛ no, a wɔn a wɔde ama a a ɛda hyɛ no (past simple) kaa no.
3. **Past Perfect** (had + participio a ɛda hyɛ no). Kyerɛ ama a ɛda hyɛ no ansa na ama biara a ɛda hyɛ no. Wɔmmusua no pɛn pɛn wɔ Spanish, nanso ɛyɛ den sɛ wubɛka ɛkɔso kronkron.
4. **'Used to'** (ɔkyerɛfoɔ + used to + ɛkɔso a ɛnyɛ kyerɛw) de ama anaa ɛkɔso a ɛda hyɛ no a ɛnyɛ nea ɛyɛ nkwa.
5. **'Would'** de ama a ɛda hyɛ no (wɔ kyerɛw a ɛyɛ kronkron anaa a wɔde no asɛm).
Kyerɛw a wɔde no hyɛ ɛkɔso: 'first', 'then', 'after that', 'suddenly', 'finally', etc. Wɔde no ma asɛm no yɛ ɛkɔso.
Mmusu: ɛkɔso a wɔn ho adanse (go-went-gone, see-saw-seen). Sɛe sɛ wɔ kyerɛkyerɛ mmienu ne kyerɛkyerɛ kɔkɔ no, yɛde 'did' ne ɛkɔso a ɛnyɛ kyerɛw.
Sɛ wɔ B1 level no, yɛnntɔn 'past perfect continuous' (ɛyɛ den pɛn pɛn).

title: Arguing a point of view / Kasa asɛm biara mu kwan
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, sɛ yɛbɛka yɛn adwene nkyɛn, yɛnka asɛm bɛka sɛ 'me maame' anaa 'me maame bɛka sɛ', na ɛsɛ sɛ yɛbɛka ɔkɔmfo no nti yɛn nhyehyɛe no ho asɛm. Wɔ English mu, ɔkɔmfo no yɛ ɔkwan ne sɛ yɛbɛka 'I think that...' anaa 'In my opinion...'. Afe a, wɔ English mu, wɔde 'should' ma ka adwene anaa apamfo, na wɔ Twi mu yɛde 'debería' anaa 'tendría que'. Hwɛ sɛ wopue 'yo pienso que' kwan kyerɛw 'I think that' (yɛ nokorɛ) nanso mma wopue ɔkɔmfo no: 'Pienso que' = 'I think that' (nnye 'Think that'). Ɛno ara nso ɛyɛ sɛ wɔde 'I am agree' nkaa 'I agree', efisɛ wɔ Twi mu 'estar de acuerdo' de 'estar' nkaa na wɔ English mu 'agree' yɛ verb a ɛnyɛ adjective.
rule:
Sɛ wubɛka w'adwene nkyɛn wɔ English mu wɔ B1 level no, hwɛ ɛno akyi:

1. **Ka w'adwene:** 'I think (that)...', 'I believe (that)...', 'In my opinion...', 'From my point of view...'. Adwene: 'I think that recycling is important.'
2. **Ma nkyɛn:** 'because', 'since', 'as'. Adwene: 'I believe we should save water because it's essential for life.'
3. **Ma apamfo anaa adwuma:** 'should' + verb (mma wode 'to'). Adwene: 'People should use public transport more.'
4. **Agree anaa disagree:** 'I agree', 'I disagree', 'I agree with you', 'I don't agree'. Hwɛ sɛ: 'agree' yɛ verb, ɛnyɛ adjective, entɛ sɛ wode 'be + agree'. Adwene: 'I agree with your idea.' (Nnye: 'I am agree').
5. **Kwan kyerɛw:** 'However', 'but', 'on the other hand'. Adwene: 'Some people think that, but I disagree.'

Hwɛ sɛ wɔ English mu ɔkɔmfo no yɛ ɔkwan, mma wɔmfa ho nhyehyɛe mu: 'I agree' nnye 'Agree'. Afe a, 'think' ne 'believe' bɛka 'that' (ɛyɛ optional) anaa wɔbɛka ɔkwan no mu kwan. Sɛ wɔ B1 no, ɛyɛ nokorɛ sɛ wode 'that' ma ɛho adanse.

title: Talking about your job and career / Kasa kwan w’awo ne kae a w’akyi
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, yɛnkyɛm ‘dɔ’ ne ‘wɔ’ de ma wɔn a wɔhyia mo asɛm so (me dɔ adwuma a ɛyɛ ɔbɛnea), nanso wɔ English mu, wɔde ‘work as’ (I work as a doctor) anaa na wɔde ‘be’ (I am a doctor) kyerɛɛ. Enti, ma yɛnnyina ‘work’ (sɛɛ adwuma) ne ‘job’ (adwuma pɛn pɛn) ho asɛm, ɛfiri sɛ wɔ Twi mu, yɛde ‘adwuma’ ma wɔn a wɔhyia. Sɛ wɔ English mu, ɛsɛ sɛ woaka subject no so (I am a doctor), nanso wɔ Twi mu, ɛnyɛ anigye sɛ woka no so (Me wɔ ɔbɛnea).
rule:
Sɛ wabɛka w’adwuma ne w’akae a w’akyi ho asɛm wɔ English mu a, hwɛ: 
- Present simple de kyerɛ w’adwuma a wɔhyia: 'I work as a teacher' anaa 'I am a teacher'.
- 'Work in' + sector anaa place (I work in a hospital), 'work for' + company (I work for Microsoft), 'work with' + people anaa things (I work with children).
- Sɛ wabɛka w’akae a w’akyi ho asɛm a, hwɛ ‘career’ (akae a w’akyi) ne ‘job’ (adwuma pɛn pɛn). Sɛ ɛba saa a, ka sɛ: 'I'm looking for a new job', 'She has a successful career'.
- Sɛ wabɛka w’adwuma a wubɛyɛ anaa w’akae a wubɛyɛ ho asɛm a, hwɛ ‘would like to’ + infinitive (I'd like to change careers) anaa ‘planning to’ (I'm planning to look for a new job).
- Hwɛ mmoa a wɔde ma adwuma a wɔhyia ho asɛm: 'always', 'usually', 'often', 'sometimes', 'never'.

title: Describing processes / Kyerɛw woɔ procesu (sɛdeɛ biribi dasani yi)
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛbɛka procesu pii wɔ  'se' passive voice (sɛ nea, 'se calienta el agua') anaa present tense. Wɔ English, wɔde 'is/are + past participle' (sɛ nea, 'the water is heated') ne sequence connectors sɛ 'first', 'then', 'next', 'after that', 'finally' hyia paa. Sɛdeɛ yɛbɛn woɔ ne sɛ, wɔ Twi yɛnntɔn subject no, noko wɔ English passive voice no, wɔde subject no anaa wɔde 'you' anaa 'they' ma yɛ impersonal form. Enti, word order wɔ English no yɛ rigid: subject, verb, na frequency adverbs no fi verb no mu bio nanso wɔde 'be' ma no.
rule: Ma wɔde B1 level no kyerɛ procesu wɔ English no, yɛde present simple (sɛ facts a ɛyɛ general) ne passive voice (present passive: am/is/are + past participle) sɛ yɛbɛma action no so sen nea ɔbɔɔ no so. Typical structure no ne: First, [object] is/are + past participle. Na yɛde sequence connectors ma no: first, then, next, after that, later, finally. Yɛmmɔɔ imperatives (sɛ instructions no mu) anaa 'you' impersonal. Passive voice no ne: subject + 'to be' verb + past participle. Sɛ nea, 'The coffee is ground.' Sɛ yɛbɛka frequency adverbs (always, usually, often) no a, ɛsɛ wɔde no fi main verb no mu bio nanso wɔde 'be' ma no (sɛ nea, 'The water is always heated first'). Wɔ English no, wɔnnyɛ 'se' ma passive voice no; wɔde passive voice wɔ 'be' anaa active form wɔ 'you' no.

title: Expressing uncertainty and possibility / Kyerɛw ka ho nhya kwan so ne nnwim
bridge: Wɔ España kasa mu, yɛnka subjunctive tense anaa mmoa kasaa ‘quizás’ ne ‘tal vez’ ma kyerɛw ka ho nhya, nanso wɔ English mu, subjunctive tense ntɛm nyɛ; na wɔn a wɔde n’awerɛho no wɔ mmoa kasaa ‘might’ ne ‘could’ anaa mmoa kasaa ‘maybe’ ne ‘perhaps’. Nya daakye: ‘must’ nni ‘debe’ ma kyerɛw nnwim, nanso kyerɛkyerɛ de ho nhya (debe de).
rule: Ma wɔde kyerɛw ka ho nhya wɔ English mu, yɛnka: 1) Mmoa kasaa: ‘maybe’, ‘perhaps’, ‘probably’, ‘definitely’ (wɔ mfonini anaa akyi a ɛbɛka ako a ɔbɛka ho asɛm no ho). 2) Mmoa kasaa: ‘may’, ‘might’, ‘could’ ma kyerɛw nnwim (may/might yɛ fɔtrɛ a wɔde bɛka ho asɛm; could yɛ mma a wɔde bɛka ho asɛm wɔ kwan so). 3) ‘Must’ ma kyerɛkyerɛ de ho nhya: ‘She must be at home’. 4) Kyerɛw ‘be likely to’ anaa ‘be unlikely to’ ma kyerɛw nnwim. Wɔ mmemmɛm, yɛnka ‘might not’ anaa ‘may not’ (nni ‘could not’ ma kyerɛw nnwim, efisɛ ‘couldn’t’ kyerɛkyerɛ a ɔno ara na ɔwɔ hɔ wɔ akannifo a ɛda paa).

common_error.explanation: Wɔ España kasa mu, wɔka ‘puede que ella venga’ na wɔtɔ ‘to’ akyi ‘may’ anaa ‘might’. Nanso wɔ English mu, akyi mmoa kasaa (may, might, could, must) no, yɛnka infinitive verb a ɛnni ‘to’. Nya daakye: modal + verb base.

levels.label: Adverbs of uncertainty
levels.translation: Mmoa kasaa a wɔde kyerɛw ka ho nhya

levels.label: Modal verbs for possibility
levels.translation: Mmoa kasaa a wɔde kyerɛw nnwim

examples.original: They might arrive late.

examples.translation: Ebia na wɔbɛba paa.
examples.note: ‘Might’ kyerɛkyerɛ nnwim a ɛnyɛ paa. Wɔ España kasa mu, ‘puede que’ + subjunctive tense.

examples.note: Mmemmɛm a wɔde bɛka ho asɛm ‘may’ no yɛ ‘may not’ (nni ‘may not’ a wɔde bɛka ho asɛm). Yɛnka ‘might not’ ma kyerɛw nnwim a ɛso.

levels.label: Deductions and probabilities
levels.translation: Kyerɛkyerɛ de ho nhya ne nnwim

examples.note: Wɔ English mu, ‘must’ wɔ kwan so a ɛyɛ fɔtrɛ no, wɔde ma kyerɛkyerɛ de ho nhya, nni a ɔbɛyɛ (nanso ɛyɛ a ɔbɛyɛ).

examples.note: Kyerɛw ‘be likely to’ + verb yɛ mma a wɔde bɛka ho asɛm wɔ nnwim a ɛyɛ fɔtrɛ.

examples.original: That won't be true.
examples.phonetic: /ðæt woʊnt bi truː/
examples.translation: Ebi nni so.
examples.note: Ma wɔde ayɛ mmemmɛm a wɔde bɛka ho asɛm akyerɛkyerɛ no, yɛnka ‘can't’ anaa ‘must not’: ‘That can't be true’.

translations.tw: Kyerɛw ka ho nhya kwan so ne nnwim

title: Making formal requests / Kyerɛw wo kwan a ɛyɛ fɔm ma no ne kyerɛw no a ɛyɛ fɔm ma no
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnkyerɛ yɛnka ‘sɛ obi bɛ...?’ anaa ‘sɛ yɛbɛ...?’ ma kyerɛw a ɛyɛ fɔm ma no. Wɔ English, na ‘Would you mind...?’ ne gerund (-ing) no sɛnea wɔde ma kyerɛw a ɛyɛ fɔm ma no, na ɛnyɛ sɛnea yɛde ma kyerɛw wɔ Twi. Ntwe ahwɛ sɛ wopue ‘Would you care...?’ sɛnea ɛyɛ wɔ Twi, efisɛ ɛte sɛ ɛfata. Nso, hwɛ sɛ wɔ English a ɛyɛ fɔm ma no, ‘please’ bɛka nea ɛwɔ hɔ akyiri anaa akyire modal verb no, ɛnyɛ sɛnea ɛyɛ wɔ Twi.
rule:
Ma kyerɛw a ɛyɛ fɔm ma no wɔ English (B1 level), hwɛ ɛnɛ ha:
1. **Would you + verb base...?** – 'Would you send me the report?' (Sɛ obi bɛma me report no?). Ɛyɛ fɔm ma na ɛte sɛ ɛfata.
2. **Could you + verb base...?** – 'Could you help me with this?' (Sɛ obi bɛkɔso me wɔ ɛyi?). Ɛte sɛ ‘Would’, noko ɛnyɛ fɔm ma paa.
3. **Would you mind + gerund (-ing)?** – 'Would you mind closing the window?' (Sɛ obi bɛyɛ me ho sɛ wɔbɔ window no?). Ɛyɛ fɔm ma paa na wɔde ma kyerɛw a ɛbɛyɛ den sɛ wɔyɛ. Sɛ ɛnyɛ wo ho a, ka ‘No, not at all.’
4. **I would like to + verb base** – 'I would like to request a refund.' (Mepɛ sɛ mebɔ kyerɛw sɛ wɔbɔ me refund.) Ma wɔkyerɛw a ɛfata wo ho.
5. **Formal questions with 'Would it be possible to...?'** – 'Would it be possible to reschedule the meeting?' (Sɛ yɛbɛtumi akyɛ meeting no?). Ɛyɛ fɔm ma paa na wɔde ma kyerɛw wɔ emails.
Hwɛ: wɔ English, ‘please’ bɛka nea ɛwɔ hɔ akyiri anaa akyire subject no wɔ kyerɛw a ɛyɛ fɔm ma no, ɛnyɛ sɛnea ɛyɛ wɔ Twi. Ɛkɔsɛe: 'Could you help me, please?' ɛnyɛ 'Please, could you help me?'.

levels.label: Basic polite requests
levels.translation: Kyerɛw a ɛyɛ fɔm ma no a ɛte sɛ ɛfata

examples.original: Could you open the door?
examples.phonetic: /kʊd juː ˈoʊpən ðə dɔːr/
examples.translation: Sɛ obi bɛbɔ door no?
examples.note: Hwɛ sɛ woka ‘could’ na wɔka ‘can’ sɛ wubɔ kyerɛw a ɛyɛ fɔm ma no.

levels.label: Formal requests with 'Would you mind'
levels.translation: Kyerɛw a ɛyɛ fɔm ma no ne 'Would you mind'

examples.original: Would you mind speaking more slowly?
examples.phonetic: /wʊd juː maɪnd ˈspiːkɪŋ mɔːr ˈsloʊli/
examples.translation: Sɛ obi bɛyɛ me ho sɛ wɔbɔ ɛkasa no pɛn pɛn?

examples.phonetic: /wʊd juː maɪnd ɪf aɪ kloʊzd ðə ˈwɪndoʊ/
examples.translation: Sɛ obi bɛyɛ me ho sɛ mɛbɔ window no?
examples.note: Sɛ woka ‘if’ no, yɛnka past simple verb sɛ yɛbɔ kyerɛw a ɛyɛ fɔm ma no.

levels.label: Written formal requests
levels.translation: Kyerɛw a ɛyɛ fɔm ma no wɔ kyerɛw a ɛyɛ fɔm ma no

examples.translation: Meda wo ase sɛ wɔbɛma me documents no.
examples.note: Ɛyɛ fɔm ma paa na wɔde ma kyerɛw wɔ emails.

examples.translation: Sɛ yɛbɛtumi akyɛ call no akyire next week?
